## Key ideas {#ss6-key-ideas .gs-lesson .gs-key-ideas}

<div class="gs-key-row">
<h3>Expansion and cancellation</h3>
$$ (x-1)(1+x+\cdots+x^{n-1})=x^n-1 $$
</div>

<div class="gs-key-row">
<h3>Finite geometric sum</h3>
$$S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}ar^{k-1}=\begin{cases}\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1},&r\ne1,\\[0.6em]na,&r=1.\end{cases}$$
</div>

<div class="gs-key-row">
<h3>When the lower bound changes</h3>
$$\sum_{k=p}^{q}ar^{k-1}:\qquad\text{first term}=ar^{p-1},\qquad N=q-p+1$$
</div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 42 · Key Ideas</p>

::: notes


Students record these results in the booklet. n is a positive integer, and p and q are positive integers with p≤q. In the final line N is the count of included terms, while a is the first term of the original sequence; substitute the first included term ar^(p−1) and N into the finite-sum formula. Count terms before selecting the formula. When r=1, use N times the first included term. The expansion identity itself is valid at x=1. Finite sums do not require |r|<1; that condition belongs to limiting sums in Lesson 7.

:::
